Bilang paggunita sa araw ng kapanganakan ni Andres Bonifacio, nagkasa ng mga pagkilos ang iba-ibang sektor sa Maynila bilang bahagi ng mas malawak na “Baha sa Luneta 2.0” rally kontra korapsyon ngayong Linggo.

Sa kabila ng panggigipit ng kapulisan dahil sa kawalan ng permit ng protesta, dahilan para maantala ang paghahanda ng stage at sound systems noong madaling araw, matagumpay na nakatungtong ang mga grupo sa Luneta Park. Giit ng BAYAN, nauna nang nakipag-ugnayan ang grupo sa lokal na pamahalaan ng Maynila at Metropolitan Manila Development Authority para sa protesta.

Inirehistro ng mga grupo ang panawagang pababain sa pwesto sina Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Bise Presidente Sara Duterte sa gitna ng kanilang pagkakasangkot sa kabi-kabilang kaso ng katiwaliaan sa pamahalaan. Pinanawagan din ng pagkilos ang pagtatag ng people’s transition council na pansamantalang pamumunuan ang bansa habang nagsasagawa ng mga repormang naka-angkla sa interes ng taumbayan.

Matapos ang programa sa Luneta, nagmartsa patungong Mendiola ang mga grupo, ngunit hinarang sila ng makapal na barikada ng kapulisan sa kalagitnaan ng Recto Ave. 

Bilang pagtatapos ng programa, winasak ng mga kalahok ang “Korapcodile,” ang dambuhalang buwayang effigy na may mukha nina Marcos Jr. at Duterte, suot ang watawat ng Estados Unidos.

#StopKorap
#KurakotManagot 

Mga kuhang larawan ni Raicelle Alvarez, Jay Janubas, Lemuel Pabalan, Lorence Lozano, Alexa Sambale, at Patrick Raphael Ulibas

CATHOLIC BISHOPS REJECT COUP OFFERS | SAYS THEY ARE NOT TEMPTED BY POSSITIONS IN GOVERNMENT | CALLS OF ARMED FORCES TO REMAIN LOYAL TO THE REPUBLIC | NO ALTERNATIVE TO DEMOCRACY SAYS CARDINAL DAVID

In a stirring speech to large crowds at the historic EDSA Shrine on Nov 30, Pablo Vigilio Cardinal David, President of Catholics Bishops Conference of the Philippines and Bishop of Kalookan, said that there is no alternative to a constitutional and democratic government and decried calls for a "reset" of the Philippines.

Cardinal David called on uniformed personal to remain loyal their out and defend Philippine democracy, calling it a path to a 'banana republic' if a coup were to take place - even if the powerful Catholic hierarchy were offered seats at a new Revolutionary Government. Cardinal David insisted that they will not be tempted by offers to lead the country as religious theocrats like the Taliban, saying the true power of the Catholic Church in the Philippines was its the moral and spiritual authority over the Filipino people.

Cardinal David then went on to say that the spirit of the EDSA Revolution was incomplete, stating that there is no alternative to democracy and admonishing calls to start from zero with the Philippine project. He went on to remind government officials and military men that they swore an oath to the 1987 Constitution and must defend it as it enters its 40 year anniversary. He said the country’s democratic system, though imperfect, is better than none and must be strengthened through citizen vigilance, legal reforms, and public participation in governance.

The outgoing president of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of the Philippines cited political dynasties as one of the “most malignant forms of cancer” in the country and urged lawmakers to pass political reforms to curb their influence, whilst strengthening legitimate political parties.

“Democracy cannot function fully until these tumors, especially political dynasties, are removed. It will take a sort of chemotherapy to eliminate these cancer cells before they metastasize,” David said.

The cardinal also addressed President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., criticizing mismanaged national budgets and urging accountability without exemptions. He challenged Marcos to ensure transparent investigations, uphold the rule of law, and complete infrastructure projects that deliver real benefits.

“Do your work,” David said, drawing loud cheers from the crowd. The Cardinal urged the President to show conviction and finish what he started to prove his worth, saying “Show us you will pursue corrupt officials impartially, wherever the trail of evidence may lead.”

Notably, Cardinal David said the Church understood that the 'UniTeam' alliance between Marcos and Duterte in 2022 wasn't meant to be, saying not all unity was a good thing and compared the breakup of the alliance to God bringing down the Tower of Babel in the Old Testament.

Cardinal David also attacked the Duterte political family,  saying the Church does not want a government that murders people in a "fake War on Drugs" like the previous administration, nor do they want a government that is ungrounded in law and respect for human dignity.

Church-backed gatherings were held in dioceses nationwide, with some holding prayer rallies the day before. David said the Metro Manila rally is part of a broader effort to uphold the enduring spirit of Edsa and resist attempts to weaken democratic gains.

He stressed that the rally also signals the Church’s rejection of “quick fixes.” “We do not need to burn down the whole house because we want to catch and hold accountable the cockroaches and rats of our society,” he added.

“How can we make the guilty pay when we are starting again from nothing?” he said, as he slammed violent rhetoric, calling people to talk with their fellow Filipinos instead of hating them.

Video Source: Philippine Daily Inquirer

Around 90,000 people joined various rallies across the country on Bonifacio Day, the Philippine National Police (PNP) said on Sunday.

As of 5 p.m., the PNP reported that 87 protest activities had ended, while 32 others were still ongoing. A total of 55,975 individuals joined the completed gatherings, and another 35,890 participated in those still underway.

Metro Manila had the largest turnout with around 16,000 participants.
